description: A heavy, very durable West African hardwood with golden-yellow to orange-brown heartwood. Used for marine work, piling, heavy construction, and hard-wearing flooring.

hazards.summary: HSE lists dermatitis among reported effects of opepe.
HSE lists irritation of the nose and throat, nose bleeds, and spitting blood among reported effects of opepe dust.
HSE also lists nervous system effects such as giddiness and changes in vision. No primary report of these effects was found during this review.
IARC classifies all wood dust as carcinogenic to humans, chiefly through cancers of the nose and sinuses. This applies to opepe dust as it does to any other wood.

image_prompt: Photorealistic studio photograph of a freshly planed opepe (Nauclea diderrichii) board, shot at a low three-quarter angle so the face grain fills most of the frame. Golden yellow to warm orange-brown heartwood that is fairly uniform in tone, with no sapwood showing. Interlocked grain producing a broad ribbon stripe, medium to coarse texture with open pores, and a moderate golden luster. Soft diffused daylight from upper left, gentle falloff, neutral warm-grey seamless background, shallow depth of field with the near edge tack-sharp. No text, no logos, no hands, no tools, no finish or varnish, natural unfinished wood. Wide 1200x630 composition (1.91:1) with the board centered and margin on both sides for cropping.
image_alt: Planed board of opepe with golden orange-brown heartwood and a broad ribbon stripe from interlocked grain.
notes_internal: Only source is HSE-WIS30. PubMed and Europe PMC searches for opepe / Nauclea diderrichii health effects found no primary reports. Common names other than 'opepe' (bilinga, badi, kusia) are trade-name knowledge not checked against a cited source; verify against BS EN 13556 or USDA FPL.
